newsitem.title: SPAIN: FOCUS-Spain's Tabacalera dumps olive-oil maker.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Spain's Tabacalera dumps olive-oil maker.

text.p: Leading Spanish tobacco group Tabacalera's sale of its stake in olive oil producer Koipe will help it concentrate on core business but cigarette price rises are still needed, analysts said on Wednesday.

Tabacalera, which is 52 percent state-owned, said it was selling its 9.66 percent stake in Koipe and was considering the sale of its 4.6 percent stake in sugar refiner Ebro. Also, the company said it may compete for the privatisation of Tabaqueira de Portugal.
Analysts praised the changes as positive in the near term but said the company would have to raise tobacco prices and diversify in the longer run due to stiff international competition.

"I think the strategy of concentrating in the tobacco sector is quite positive but it's difficult because of competition from other multinationals," said Pedro Monjardin, analyst at Spanish investment house Benito y Monjardin.
Tabacalera posted a disappointing 10.8 percent rise in first half net profits, hurt by a summer price war after a surprise government cigarette tax hike in July.
The new government, pressed to cover a huge shortfall in the 1995 budget, raised taxes on cigarettes and alcohol.

Tabacalera responded by putting up prices on its black tobacco, a primarily domestic market. But until now it has not passed on the price rises in Virginia or blonde tobacco to retain market share in the more competitive international arena.

"The biggest question about Tabacalera is whether they are going to increase prices to pass part of the increase in taxes on to the consumer," said a Spain market analyst at Banque Paribas in London. "That would help the margins of the company."
He said the sale of Koipe would be healthy if the cash goes to restructure the core tobacco business.
A member of the board of directors said capital gains from the sale would be 200 million pesetas ($1.57 million).
Monjardin estimated market value of the Ebro stake around 3.2 billion pesetas.
"The idea is to clean up the balance sheet and take out all non-strategic investments," said Monjardin.

In the competition for Tabaqueira de Portugal, Tabacalera will have to battle multinational giants eager to expand into markets with lax tobacco legislation amid a strident anti-cigarette campaign in the United States.
The tax hike in July depressed Tabacalera's share price but it has been recovering since early this month, analysts said.
Monjardin said his company changed their sell recommendation on Tabacalera to a neutral about two weeks ago.
